p.src: A massless particle has no rest frame. Its invariant spin label is helicity, the angular momentum along its direction of motion. A photon has only $h=+1$ and $h=-1$; a graviton has only $h=+2$ and $h=-2$. A scalar has one $h=0$ state. The lecture uses reflection symmetry to pair the two helicities. In a chiral theory a single massless irreducible representation may carry only one helicity, so the pairing is an additional symmetry statement rather than a consequence of masslessness alone.

Consequently every consistent interacting closed-string theory contains gravity.
